LESSON: ENLIGHTENED BEINGS AND SOCIAL WELFARE

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Enlightened Beings
Topic 2.1: Enlightened Beings and Social Welfare
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Enlightened Beings and Social Welfare, part of The Enlightened Beings in Grade 5 HINDU RELIGIOUS EDUCATION.

Key inquiry question: How do Enlightened Beings contribute to social welfare? 2. How do we emulate the Enlightened Beings in our lives?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read the life histories of the four Enlightened Beings and social welfare,

2. listen to stories of Enlightened Beings using Scriptures/a resource person/audio-visual device,

3. research and write assays on the lives of Enlightened Beings and present their research in class,

4. perform skits based on the key events from the lives of Enlightened Beings,

5. draw sketches of Enlightened Beings using digital devices/drawing book,

6. make a chart of the teachings and reforms of the Enlightened Beings,

7. take part in quiz competitions,

8. watch animated films on Enlightened Beings using digital devices,

9. engage and encourage peers with special needs to sing songs/bhajan/stavan/shabad that glorify the qualities of Enlightened Beings. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read the life histories of the four Enlightened Beings and social welfare,
2. listen to stories of Enlightened Beings using Scriptures/a resource person/audio-visual device,
3. research and write assays on the lives of Enlightened Beings and present their research in class,
4. perform skits based on the key events from the lives of Enlightened Beings,
5. draw sketches of Enlightened Beings using digital devices/drawing book,
6. make a chart of the teachings and reforms of the Enlightened Beings,
7. take part in quiz competitions,
8. watch animated films on Enlightened Beings using digital devices,
9. engage and encourage peers with special needs to sing songs/bhajan/stavan/shabad that glorify the qualities of Enlightened Beings. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Enlightened Beings and Social Welfare together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: Learner enhances networking when performing skits based on the key events from the lives of

Enlightened Beings.

Values:
● Unity: Learner enhances cooperation when drawing sketches of Enlighted Beings using digital devices/drawing book.

● Responsibility: Learner acquires virtues of hard work when developing charts of the teachings and reforms of the

Enlightened Beings.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Citizenship: Learner develops social cohesion by engaging and encouraging peers with special needs to sing

songs/bhajan/stavan/shabad that glorify the qualities of Enlightened Beings.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Learner is able to relate the skill of making sketches, singing bhajans, mantras and hymns to the skills of similar creative

activities in Creative Arts.

The learner is able to relate the encouragement to study life histories of Enlightened Beings to the skills of studying life histories

learnt in Social Studies.
